question: The majority of regulatory T lymphocytes express high levels of:

options.opc: The alpha chain of the receptor for IL-2.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Molecules of the B7 family -> Regulatory T lymphocytes express high levels -> 80% CHAIN: The alpha chain of the receptor for IL-2 -> Regulatory T lymphocytes express high levels -> 85% CHAIN: CD8 -> Not expressed at high levels by regulatory T lymphocytes -> Unclear -> 70% CHAIN: IL-17 -> Not expressed at high levels by regulatory T lymphocytes -> 75% CHAIN: Perforin -> Not expressed at high levels by regulatory T lymphocytes -> 80%
enhanced_information: Regulatory T lymphocytes express high levels of the alpha chain of the receptor for IL-2. This is supported by the interaction between Interleukin-2 and Regulatory T-Lymphocytes. Molecules of the B7 family are also expressed at high levels by regulatory T lymphocytes.
analysis: Regulatory T lymphocytes are known to express high levels of the alpha chain of the receptor for IL-2, which is a key feature of their function. Additionally, they also express molecules of the B7 family. While both options are supported by enhanced information, the primary marker associated with regulatory T lymphocytes is the alpha chain of the receptor for IL-2.
